text:
mira: Heads-up — Console latency heatmap is misleading when comparing endpoints. We use a global color scale so tiny p50 differences look huge across rows. Example: endpoint A p50=120ms vs endpoint B p50=140ms and the color jumps from green to red, folks assume a regression. Screenshot: https://fake.corp/snap/heatmap-1.png

alex: I noticed that too. Global scale was intentional to make p99 spikes pop, but it does make cross-row comparisons noisy during rollouts.

sam: Figma mock for a per-row normalization mode: https://figma.com/file/xyz. Also thinking a toggle (Absolute / Relative color modes) could be low-friction.

jordan: Careful — per-row normalization will hide systemic shifts (if everything shifts right, relative view looks unchanged). We should preserve a global signal somewhere.

mira: Agreed. Proposal: default stays global (so system regressions remain obvious) + add a compact per-row relative heatmap or a percent-change overlay next to p50 p95 columns. That gives both perspectives.

alex: Also, we get false alarms when sample counts are tiny. Can we surface sample_count in the cell tooltip or a little badge so people don't overreact to low-sample color changes?

devex: From UX perspective — keep red meaning 'bad for the whole system'. Idea: heatmap color = global z-score buckets, but show a tiny inline sparkline normalized to the row underneath. Users get both global severity and local shape.

sam: Implementation note: frontend would want an endpoint for row stats: min/max/mean/std to compute relative buckets client-side. Backend could optionally return per-row summary in the rollup payload.

jordan: Backend constraints: we already return p50/p95/p99/count per endpoint/window. Adding mean/std/min/max increases payload but we can gate it behind a query param like `include_stats=true`. That keeps the default cheap.

sam: Example query snippet we'd use server-side for the on-demand stats:```
SELECT endpoint, window_start, p50, p95, p99, count, avg_latency, stddev_latency, min_latency, max_latency
FROM endpoint_latency_rollup
WHERE window='5m' AND region='us-west';
```

alex: If we add include_stats flag, can we avoid doubling the aggregation cost? Jordan, is that async or cheap?

jordan: It is a bit heavier but still within our rollup job. We can materialize the extra fields at rollup time; storage delta is small. Cost impact is ~5-10% on ingestion compute for that table. Fine if opt-in at query time.

mira: Ok — roadmap: 1) add `include_stats` opt-in to rollup API, 2) frontend toggle: Global vs Relative (default Global), 3) add sample_count badge and tooltip copy clarifying low-sample caveat, 4) small percent-delta column for p50. Can we aim for a staging deploy next week?

deploy-bot: deploy queued: frontend/heatmap-toggle -> staging (build #4721)

sam: I'll open the PR today and link the Figma. Will tag @devex for copy on the tooltip.

mira: Thanks — this should cut down on misleading alerts during canaries. :thumbsup:
